en.title: When patients stop being measured: how much does dropout change a tumor-shrinkage estimate?
en.summary: Most tumor-scan dropout was death. A mixed model removed most of the survivor bias in 48-week shrinkage; a joint model and delta adjustment showed the 24-week arm difference was robust but the 48-week difference was fragile.
key_findings: In a public colorectal-cancer subset where most scan dropout was death, the mean of patients still scanned overstated 48-week shrinkage by about a third in the combination arm; a mixed-effects model removed most of that bias.
The 24-week shrinkage and arm difference held under every dropout assumption tried, including a joint model and delta adjustments.
The 48-week arm difference lost support if dropouts in the better-looking arm deteriorated about 0.5 per year faster than predicted; without recorded dropout reasons, the mechanism is not identified.
